quests.instruction: The dentist says you have no cavities after all that worrying. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Hearing good news you were nervous about can make your whole body feel lighter.
quests.explanation: Hearing good news you were nervous about hearing makes your whole body feel lighter.
quests.funFact: Brushing twice a day is one of the best ways to hear this kind of good news at every checkup!

quests.instruction: You watch a robot solve a puzzle cube in just a few seconds. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Watching a machine do something incredibly fast can leave you staring in wonder.
quests.explanation: Watching a machine do something incredibly fast can leave you with a wide-eyed, astonished feeling.
quests.funFact: The fastest puzzle-solving robots can finish a scrambled cube in under a single second!

quests.instruction: You make a get-well card for a friend who is out sick. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Making something thoughtful for someone who needs cheering up feels warm and kind.
quests.explanation: Making something thoughtful for someone who needs cheering up gives you a warm, kind feeling.
quests.funFact: Studies show that receiving a handmade card can genuinely help someone feel a little better!

quests.instruction: You decide to keep trying until you can finally whistle. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Choosing to keep going toward a goal, even when it is tricky, feels strong and focused.
quests.explanation: Choosing to keep going toward a tricky goal gives you a strong, focused feeling.
quests.funFact: Whistling uses very small, precise muscles in your lips — it often takes lots of practice!

quests.instruction: You keep asking when it will finally be your turn on the swing. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Wanting your turn to come faster than it is coming can feel very restless.
quests.explanation: Wanting your turn to come faster than it is coming can give you a restless, waiting feeling.
quests.funFact: Counting to a certain number together is a fun way many kids make turn-taking feel fair and fast!

quests.instruction: You are about to try a new food you have never tasted before. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Trying something completely unfamiliar for the first time can make your stomach flutter.
quests.explanation: Trying something completely unfamiliar for the first time can give you a fluttery feeling.
quests.funFact: Trying new foods more than once often helps them start to taste more familiar and less new!

quests.instruction: You accidentally send a text message to the wrong person. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Realizing a message went to the wrong place can make your cheeks feel warm.
quests.explanation: Realizing a message went to the wrong place can make your cheeks feel warm and a little shy.
quests.funFact: Double-checking a name before sending is a simple habit that can help prevent this mix-up!

quests.instruction: You do not get chosen as line leader even though you raised your hand first. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Not getting a small role you really wanted can leave you with a heavy feeling.
quests.explanation: Not getting a small role you really wanted can leave you with a heavy, letdown feeling.
quests.funFact: Teachers usually give everyone a turn to lead the line eventually — yours will come soon!

quests.instruction: Your bus driver waits an extra moment when they see you running late. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Someone doing a small kind thing just for you can fill your heart with warmth.
quests.explanation: Someone doing a small kind thing just for you fills your heart with a warm, grateful feeling.
quests.funFact: Waving and saying thank you to a bus driver is a simple way to brighten their day too!

quests.instruction: Your friend's science project gets a bigger reaction from the class than yours. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Watching someone else's work get more attention than yours can feel uncomfortable.
quests.explanation: Watching someone else's work get more attention than yours can give you an uncomfortable, wanting feeling.
quests.funFact: Every project teaches something new, even ones that do not get the biggest reaction!

quests.instruction: You realize the noise that scared you last night was just the wind. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Finding out something that worried you has a simple, harmless explanation can feel very settling.
quests.explanation: Finding out something that worried you has a simple explanation makes your whole body feel lighter.
quests.funFact: Wind can make many different sounds, from whistles to creaks, depending on what it blows past!

quests.instruction: You see the biggest waterfall you have ever seen in person. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Seeing something in nature that is far bigger than you imagined can leave you speechless.
quests.explanation: Seeing something in nature far bigger than you imagined can leave you with an astonished feeling.
quests.funFact: The tallest waterfalls in the world drop taller than many skyscrapers!

quests.instruction: You share your umbrella with a classmate caught in the rain. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Helping someone else stay comfortable, even if it means sharing, feels warm and kind.
quests.explanation: Helping someone else stay comfortable, even if it means sharing, gives you a warm, kind feeling.
quests.funFact: Small, simple acts of sharing are one of the easiest ways to show kindness every day!

quests.instruction: You keep rereading the hard chapter until you finally understand it. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Refusing to give up on something confusing until it makes sense feels strong and focused.
quests.explanation: Refusing to give up on something confusing until it makes sense gives you a strong, focused feeling.
quests.funFact: Rereading a tricky part is something even strong readers do — it is a smart, normal strategy!

quests.instruction: You keep peeking out the window waiting for your friend to arrive. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Watching and waiting for someone to show up can make you check again and again.
quests.explanation: Watching and waiting for someone to show up can give you a restless, waiting feeling.
quests.funFact: Finding a small task to do while you wait can help the minutes go by much faster!

quests.instruction: You are waiting for your name to be called to receive an award. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Waiting to be called up in front of a crowd can make your hands feel a little shaky.
quests.explanation: Waiting to be called up in front of a crowd can give you a shaky, fluttery feeling.
quests.funFact: Taking a slow breath while you wait can help this fluttery feeling settle before your name is called.

quests.instruction: You realize you have been wearing mismatched shoes all day. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Noticing a silly mistake others may have seen can make your cheeks feel warm.
quests.explanation: Noticing a silly mistake others may have seen can make your cheeks feel warm and a little shy.
quests.funFact: Mismatched shoes are actually a fun fashion trend for some people — it is nothing to worry about!

quests.instruction: Your favorite flavor of ice cream is sold out at the shop. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Looking forward to a favorite treat and finding it unavailable can leave you feeling let down.
quests.explanation: Looking forward to a favorite treat and finding it unavailable can leave you feeling let down.
quests.funFact: Trying a brand-new flavor can sometimes turn into a fun surprise discovery!

quests.instruction: A classmate helps you clean up spilled paint without being asked. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Someone helping you out of a messy moment without being asked can fill your heart with warmth.
quests.explanation: Someone helping you out of a messy moment without being asked fills you with a warm, grateful feeling.
quests.funFact: Helping without being asked is one of the kindest and most thoughtful things a friend can do!

quests.instruction: Your classmate gets to sit in the special reading chair every single day. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Watching someone else always get a special turn can feel uncomfortable.
quests.explanation: Watching someone else always get a special turn can give you an uncomfortable, wanting feeling.
quests.funFact: Asking a teacher calmly about turn-taking is a great way to help make things feel fair.

quests.instruction: The rain stops just in time for the outdoor event to continue as planned. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Watching a worry about your plans fade away can make your shoulders drop and relax.
quests.explanation: Watching a worry about your plans fade away makes your shoulders drop and your body feel lighter.
quests.funFact: Weather can change quickly, which is why outdoor plans often have a backup plan just in case!

quests.instruction: You see a real rainbow stretching all the way across the sky. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Seeing something huge and beautiful in nature can leave you staring in wonder.
quests.explanation: Seeing something huge and beautiful in nature can leave you with a wide-eyed, astonished feeling.
quests.funFact: A full rainbow that stretches into a complete circle can sometimes be seen from an airplane!

quests.instruction: You help your tired mom by putting your little sister's toys away. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Doing a helpful task without being asked, to make someone's day easier, feels warm and kind.
quests.explanation: Doing a helpful task without being asked to make someone's day easier gives you a warm, kind feeling.
quests.funFact: Noticing when someone is tired and helping without being asked is a real sign of thoughtfulness!

quests.instruction: You keep working on your project even though the deadline feels far away. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Choosing to work steadily toward a goal, even without pressure, feels strong and focused.
quests.explanation: Choosing to work steadily toward a goal, even without pressure, gives you a strong, focused feeling.
quests.funFact: Working a little bit at a time, instead of all at once, often leads to your very best work!

quests.instruction: You keep glancing at the clock during the last few minutes of school. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Watching the clock and wishing the minutes would move faster feels very restless.
quests.explanation: Watching the clock and wishing the minutes would move faster gives you a restless, waiting feeling.
quests.funFact: Time can feel like it moves slower when we keep checking it — many people notice this!

quests.instruction: You finally find your lost dog waiting safely by the front door. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Having a worry suddenly disappear can make your whole body feel lighter.
quests.explanation: Having a worry suddenly disappear, like finding a lost pet safe, makes your whole body feel lighter.
quests.funFact: Your body can feel physically lighter the moment a big worry finally goes away!

quests.instruction: You see the sky fill with thousands of stars on a clear night. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Looking up and seeing far more stars than usual can leave you completely still with wonder.
quests.explanation: Looking up and seeing far more stars than usual can leave you with a wide-eyed, astonished feeling.
quests.funFact: On a truly dark, clear night, the human eye can spot thousands of individual stars!

quests.instruction: You gently help an injured bird find a safe, quiet spot in the yard. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Helping a small creature that cannot help itself feels warm and kind.
quests.explanation: Helping a small creature that cannot help itself gives you a warm, kind feeling.
quests.funFact: Giving injured wildlife a quiet, safe space and telling a grown-up is the best way to help them!

quests.instruction: You promise yourself you will finish the puzzle no matter how long it takes. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Setting your mind firmly on finishing something can feel strong and focused.
quests.explanation: Setting your mind firmly on finishing something gives you a strong, focused feeling.
quests.funFact: Breaking a big puzzle into smaller sections is a clever trick that keeps this focused feeling going!

quests.instruction: You tap your pencil while waiting for the teacher to hand back the tests. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Waiting to find out news you are eager for can make you fidget in your seat.
quests.explanation: Waiting to find out news you are eager for can give you a restless, waiting feeling.
quests.funFact: Taking a slow breath while you wait can help this restless, fidgety feeling settle a little.
